evidence: src/application/GetProductStockUseCase.ts: constructor(private productRepository: ProductRepository) depends on a repository abstraction, so there is no persistence code here
execute(): calls productRepository.findById, throws 'Product ${productId} not found' if nothing comes back, and maps the result to a ProductStockResponse DTO. This is application orchestration.
executeAll(): calls productRepository.all() and maps each product to a DTO with no business calculation
Stock comes from the domain entity's product.getStock(), so the business rule stays in the domain
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is in the application layer, and everything it does fits that layer's role. GetProductStockUseCase gets the ProductRepository abstraction through its constructor. It loads products through that abstraction and calls the domain entity's own getStock() method. It throws a "not found" error and maps the entities to ProductStockResponse DTOs. That is standard use-case orchestration plus DTO mapping. The file has no persistence code, no transport or HTTP handling and no framework logic, so it carries none of the infrastructure kind's responsibilities. It also doesn't calculate stock itself or enforce any invariants that belong in the domain; it hands that to product.getStock().
